chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The insulter of the believer is like one on the verge of destruction.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of insulting a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kulayni’s foundational *Al-Kafi*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the grave spiritual peril of insulting a believer, likening it to standing on the brink of destruction. In Shia scholarly tradition, this metaphor highlights that such an act not only damages social harmony but also jeopardizes the insulter’s own salvation, serving as a critical ethical guideline for maintaining communal unity.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The insulter of the Momin is like one on the verge of the destruction’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Reviling a believer is like one’s positioning one’s self at the verge of destruction. ’”
